sender.en: A new friend or match on Facebook, Instagram or Snapchat

name.en: Sextortion: “pay or I’ll send your photos to your friends”

how.en: A stranger, often with a fake profile of a young woman, starts chatting on social media and quickly turns the talk sexual. They suggest a video call or swapping intimate images, often after moving to another app. Once they have images, they threaten to send them to your friends and family unless you pay, and may say you committed a crime. Most victims are young men, and the offenders are usually overseas.

text.en: A stranger with an attractive profile messages you and quickly turns the chat sexual.
They ask to move to another app and to swap intimate photos or videos.
They threaten to send the images to your contacts or post them online.
They demand money, and may say you have committed a crime.
I have recorded everything. I have your friends and family list. Send $5000 now or I share the video with all of them. You have 30 minutes.

A stranger moves quickly to sexual talk.
They want to move to another app.
Their profile or language doesn’t add up, or they won’t use a webcam.
Threats and a deadline to pay.
Don’t pay and don’t send more images, even if they threaten you.
Stop replying, save the chats and take screenshots.
Block the profile and report it to the platform.
Tell someone you trust, and report it to Police or Netsafe. You won’t be in trouble.
If you or someone else is in danger, call 111.
